Knox test of space-time interaction

Source: R/knox.R
knox_test.Rd

Tests whether the cases are closer in space and time than expected if space and time were independent (Knox 1964), and returns the pairs of cases close in both (the space-time links that form the transmission chains).

Usage

knox_test(x, crs, dt, ds, sym, sp_link, planar_coord)

knox(...)

Arguments

x

a data frame with the coordinates of the cases (`x`, `y`) and the date of onset of symptoms (`onset`, a `Date` or a number).

crs

the projected coordinate reference system used to measure the distances (for example `"+proj=eqc"`, in metres).

dt

the time window: two cases are close in time when their onsets are at most `dt` apart (days if `onset` is a `Date`).

ds

the space window: two cases are close in space when they are at most `ds` apart (units of `crs`, or of the coordinates if `planar_coord = TRUE`).

sym

the number of Monte Carlo permutations.

sp_link

logical. If `TRUE` the space-time links are built with sp, else with sf.

planar_coord

logical. If `FALSE`, `x` and `y` are longitude and latitude (EPSG:4326) and are projected to `crs`; if `TRUE`, they are already planar coordinates.

...

arguments passed to `knox_test()`.

Value

A list with four elements: - `knox`, a list with the test:

knox

Knox statistic: number of pairs of cases close in space and time.

p_value

Monte Carlo p-value, \((m + 1)/(sym + 1)\), where \(m\) is the number of permutations of the onsets with at least `knox` pairs.

RR

observed pairs divided by the mean of the permutations.

expected

expected pairs, `pairs_space * pairs_time / pairs` (Knox 1964; Tango 2010).

RR_expected

observed pairs divided by `expected`.

p_poisson

Poisson mid-p-value of `knox` with mean `expected`, as in Tango (2010).

pairs

total number of pairs of cases, \(n(n - 1)/2\).

pairs_space

pairs of cases close in space.

pairs_time

pairs of cases close in time.

- `st_link`, a data frame with one row per space-time link and the coordinates of its two cases (`Xo`, `Yo`, `Xd`, `Yd`). - `x`, the cases with the planar coordinates. - `space_time_link`, an sf object (LINESTRING, EPSG:4326) with the space-time links.

Details

Two cases are close in space when their distance is at most `ds`, and close in time when their onsets are at most `dt` apart, as in the tables of Tango (2010). The test gives two p-values: the Monte Carlo p-value (the onsets are permuted among the cases `sym` times), and the Poisson mid-p-value used by Knox (1964) and Tango (2010), which is an approximation that can be misleading when the expected number of pairs is not small (Barton and David 1966).

`knox()` is the former name of `knox_test()`; it still works but it is deprecated, because it has the same name as the function of the knox package.

References

Knox EG (1964). The detection of space-time interactions. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C*, 13(1), 25-30.

Tango T (2010). *Statistical Methods for Disease Clustering*. Springer.

See also

[kaposi_uganda] for the example of Tango (2010), and [transmission_chains_map()].

Author

Felipe Antonio Dzul Manzanilla felipe.dzul.m@gmail.com

Examples

# Kaposi's sarcoma in Uganda (Tango 2010, Table 7.7): 5 km and same year
k <- knox_test(x = kaposi_uganda, crs = NULL, ds = 5, dt = 0, sym = 999,
               sp_link = FALSE, planar_coord = TRUE)
k$knox
